findings.title: Docker Hub security advisory: personal access tokens transferred during account-to-organization conversions
findings.summary_md: Docker CISO Mark Lechner confirmed that account-to-organization conversions reassigned the converted account's personal access tokens to the newly named owner without rotating the secret or asking consent, a behavior present since August 26, 2024. The report arrived September 30, 2026 and a production fix shipped the same day in under four hours; exposed users were notified October 2 and transferred PATs were force-deactivated October 8. Docker reviewed every conversion in the window and about 304,000 pushes made with transferred tokens, finding no evidence of exploitation.

findings.title: GhostPat: a ghost token in your Docker account
findings.summary_md: Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com describe how a throwaway Docker Hub account converted to an organization with a target named as owner yields a token that authenticates as that target, which they used to push to the target's namespace and pull the target's private repositories with no notification to the victim. First reproduction on 2026-09-28, a second independent reproduction on 2026-09-29, report to security@docker.com on 2026-09-30. They also flag, unconfirmed, a worst case in which the official library images sit in the same conversion path. The page carries no publish time of day; its footer states updated 2026-10-13.
